summary.text: The council's Flood Plains layer covers 51.2% of this parcel and its Flood Prone Areas layer covers 50.8%, and a mapped overland flow path also crosses it.

Your loan counts as high-LVR lending (LVR, the loan-to-value ratio, is the share of the price you borrow), which the Reserve Bank lets banks offer only in limited amounts, and its explainer says that with less than a 20% deposit you may pay higher interest rates and fees.

A First Home Loan scenario is also included because your household income is within the Kāinga Ora cap; the Kāinga Ora brochure lists a 1.2% Lender's Mortgage Insurance premium as a requirement, and Kāinga Ora states that after 1 July 2025 the Government will not fund part of that premium.

LINZ records the title as Freehold, which Settled.govt.nz says means you own the land and (generally) anything built on it, while the council valuation describes the land use as Recreational - vacant and the improvements as RESERVE LAND.
The year built could not be checked because the council's property category for this address has no build decade, and no free public source has the cladding.

next_steps.text: Ask the council or a drainage engineer whether the mapped overland flow path crosses this property and what the mapping means for it.
Ask insurers about past claims and flood exclusions before making an offer.
Ask your lawyer to obtain and review the LIM report and other property documents from the council.
Ask your lender how it applies the low-deposit lending limit and what extra costs apply.
Ask each lender what interest rate and fees apply at your deposit level.
Ask your lender which lending criteria it applies to First Home Loan applications.
Ask your lender how the First Home Loan premium would apply to your loan amount.
Check the First Home Loan criteria with a participating lender.
Check the First Home Loan income criteria with a participating lender.
Check with a participating lender how your before-tax income from the last 12 months is assessed.
Ask your lawyer to check the record of title for registered interests.
Ask a registered valuer about a current market valuation.
Ask your lender what insurance evidence it requires and get insurance quotes early.
Check your private insurance policy for cover above the Natural Hazards Commission cap.
Ask your insurer and the Natural Hazards Commission which parts of the land are covered.
Ask your insurer about its own excess in addition to the Natural Hazards Commission excess.
Ask your insurer how the Natural Hazards Insurance levy appears in the quoted premium.
Check the council property file for geotechnical reports, or ask a geotechnical engineer for site-specific advice.
Ask your lender and lawyer what finance and insurance arrangements to confirm for an auction.
